structure.summary: The chapter opens with the narrator, Montresor, vowing revenge against Fortunato for an unspecified insult, determined to punish him with impunity during the chaos of the carnival season. At dusk, Montresor encounters Fortunato, who is drunkenly dressed in a jester's motley, and cunningly lures him into the Montresor family catacombs under the pretense of tasting a pipe of rare Amontillado. Guided by Montresor, they descend through damp, bone-strewn vaults, with Fortunato growing increasingly affected by the nitre-laden air and his own intoxication; Montresor repeatedly feigns concern for his health, offering wine to keep him compliant. Once deep within a hidden recess, Montresor chains Fortunato to the wall and begins sealing him alive behind a brick-and-mortar wall, methodically building it tier by tier as Fortunato’s initial laughter turns to desperate cries and finally silence. After completing the wall and restoring the pile of bones to conceal it, Montresor declares that for half a century no one has disturbed the site, ending with the Latin phrase 'In pace requiescat.'

plot_summary.plot_summary:
Montresor, driven by a deep-seated grudge over an unspecified insult from Fortunato, resolves to exact revenge with perfect impunity during the chaotic carnival season. He meticulously plans his scheme, exploiting Fortunato’s pride as a connoisseur of wine and his intoxicated state to lure him into the Montresor family catacombs under the false pretense of sampling a rare Amontillado. With calculated charm and feigned concern, Montresor guides the unsuspecting Fortunato deeper into the damp, bone-choked vaults, offering wine to keep him docile and disoriented as the air grows thick with nitre and his own drunkenness intensifies.

As they descend into the labyrinthine depths, Montresor’s demeanor remains calm and paternal, masking his malevolent intent. He continues to play the concerned host, even as Fortunato’s coughs and stumbling steps betray his deteriorating condition. The turning point arrives when they reach a secluded niche in the catacombs; here, Montresor chains Fortunato to the wall with cold precision, revealing the true purpose of their journey. Fortunato’s initial laughter and disbelief swiftly give way to panicked screams as he realizes the horrifying truth — he is to be entombed alive.

Montresor then methodically constructs a brick-and-mortar wall, layer by layer, as Fortunato’s cries escalate into desperate pleas and finally fall into silence. Once the wall is complete and the pile of bones restored to conceal his crime, Montresor stands over his handiwork, declaring that for fifty years no one has disturbed the site. His chilling final words, 'In pace requiescat,' underscore his cold satisfaction and the eternal secrecy of his perfect revenge.
